## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art monster-catching game inspired by Pokémon Yellow.

## Requirements
- Deliver the playable game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Created an original “Pocket Trails — Yellow Day” adventure with an original Voltkit companion and creature designs.
- Implemented a compact top-down town, exploration, NPC dialogue, grass encounters, turn-based battles, and collecting a creature.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive game page, styling, pixel-art canvas scenes, keyboard and touch controls, companion/team UI, dialogue, battles, and capture mechanics.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started a local server on port 3002 and used Chromium/Playwright to load and exercise the game; no page errors were reported.

### Active
- Validate gameplay flow and fix any issues found. Quick NPC navigation tests did not reach Professor Fern; the status remained “NOTHING HERE BUT SUNSHINE AND THE SOUND OF THE BREEZE.”
- Complete the requested visual check by saving and inspecting a small JPEG screenshot; current screenshots were inspected as PNG/JPEG under `/tmp`, but `screenshots/latest.jpg` was not created because image conversion tools were unavailable.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli open` could not run because its bundled Chromium was missing; attempted installation was not performed. System Chromium at `/usr/bin/chromium` worked through Playwright.
- JPEG conversion failed because Python Pillow and `convert` were unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` map coordinates, collision, and movement to make reaching and interacting with Professor Fern reliable.
2. Run a longer automated browser playthrough covering NPC dialogue and grass encounters/battles.
3. Save and inspect a JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px using an available conversion method.
4. Summarize the finished game and note the assumption that it uses original creature names/art rather than Pokémon assets.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game layout, canvas, controls, team status, and quest UI.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch control layout.
- `game.js`: Game logic, pixel art, movement, dialogue, encounters, and battles.
- `screenshots/`: Created for visual checks; expected JPEG screenshot is not yet present.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `game.js` passed syntax checking; initial and map screenshots rendered successfully under system Chromium.

- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art monster-catching game inspired by Pokémon Yellow.

- Deliver the playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

- The game is an original adventure, “Pocket Trails — Yellow Day,” with original creatures and names, including Voltkit.
- The requested story direction is Team Rocket, starting as a grunt.

- Built a responsive game page with pixel-art scenes, town exploration, NPC dialogue, grass encounters, turn-based battles, creature capture, keyboard controls, and touch controls.

- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art monster-catching game inspired by Pokémon Yellow, with an original Team Rocket story where the player starts as a grunt.

## Requirements
- Deliver the playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

- The game is an original adventure, “Pocket Trails — Yellow Day,” with original creatures and names, including Voltkit.
- The story should center on Team Rocket, with the player beginning as a grunt.

## Work State
### Completed
- A separate `game.js` contains a pixel-art town, exploration, dialogue, encounters, turn-based battles, creature capture, keyboard controls, and touch controls.

### Active
- Establish which game implementation is served and adapt the actual app’s title, story, dialogue, UI, and progression to the Team Rocket grunt premise.
- Validate a full browser playthrough through battle actions and capture, then save and inspect an updated JPEG.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Current page markup; loads `src/main.js` and contains Kanto explorer branding.
- `src/main.js`: Active application entry point and NPC interaction logic.
- `src/kanto-data.js`: Kanto NPC dialogue, region data, and signs.
- `game.js`: Separate pixel-art monster-catching implementation with incompatible expected DOM IDs.
- `styles.css`: Styling for the Kanto explorer app.
- `style.css`: Styling for the separate game layout.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Existing screenshot from earlier visual checks.

- Changes are uncommitted; repository contains untracked project files.

- Earlier `playwright-cli open` failed because its bundled Chromium was missing; system Chromium worked through Playwright.
- Python Pillow and ImageMagick `convert` were unavailable; Playwright directly saved the prior JPEG.
